baseline_models.focus_anchor: تَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا ... مَا هُم مِّنكُمْ وَلَا مِنْهُمْ
baseline_models.mechanism: Tawalli supplies active loyalty and nearness to a qawm, while the double negation withholds membership in either camp. The affiliation therefore works across a social boundary without resolving it.

activation_trace.role: Love, support, and alliance make tawalli an enacted patronage relation rather than passive contact.
The human group image supplies the corporate body toward which loyalty is directed.

changed_reading.before: They merely befriend a hostile people.
changed_reading.after: They install a patronage tie across a boundary while remaining disowned by both named collectivities.

baseline_models.mechanism: Half spans both swearing and covenantal alliance. Placed over known falsehood, the oath is not only bad information; it is speech used to manufacture commitment and usable credibility.

activation_trace.role: The explicit oath image supplies the high-commitment speech act.
Covenant and mutual adherence give the oath a bond-making social function.
Contradiction of truth makes the bond's asserted basis false.
Disclosure to the knower makes the false performance deliberate.

changed_reading.before: They reinforce a lie by swearing to it.
changed_reading.after: They knowingly use an oath as relational technology, trying to make a false claim carry the force of a bond.

baseline_models.mechanism: The alerting question addresses an observer while the close attributes knowledge to the actors. Their inward awareness and the reader's invited recognition form a double-knowledge scene in which concealment is already exposed.

activation_trace.role: The alerting and inquiring use of 'have you seen' summons recognition of a case.
Their own disclosed knowledge supplies the inner cognitive layer set against public recognition.

changed_reading.before: The opening simply asks whether the addressee noticed these people.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages counter-recognition: observers are taught to see a performance whose performers already know its falsity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier denied motherhood formula distinguishes a spoken relational label from the birth relation it claims, then calls the utterance false. That mechanism revises the focus oath and affiliation into a second attempt to recategorize relations by speech: the oath projects belonging, while 'neither of you nor of them' refuses the projected category.

activation_trace.role: Alliance supplies the relation that the actors are trying to make socially effective.
The covenant branch lets the oath function as an attempted bond rather than bare description.
Falsehood marks the mismatch between the performed relation and the stated social reality.
Motherhood supplies the relational status that the earlier formula falsely assigns.
Descent by birth supplies the nonverbal relation against which the spoken reassignment fails.
False and void speech names the counterfeit status-making operation.

structural_cues: 58:2 first denies that a formula makes wives into mothers, identifies actual mothers by birth, and then calls the utterance objectionable and false.
58:14 likewise places an oath-built affiliation beside an explicit denial of membership in either group.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two speech acts, a denied relational status, birth as its counter-test, and explicit falsehood; I infer a shared arrow from formula to attempted social recategorization. A live alternative is that the focus oath only conceals an alliance already made rather than trying to constitute it.

changed_reading.before: The oath covers a dubious political association.
changed_reading.after: The oath participates in relational counterfeiting: it tries to give an affiliation the status of belonging that the double negation denies.

context_deltas.mechanism: The actors' knowledge in the focus is immediate and tactical, but the earlier accounting scene separates that local awareness from durable memory: deeds can be counted by God, forgotten by their doers, and retained under witness. Knowing the lie therefore does not imply control of its record or consequences.

activation_trace.role: Their knowledge supplies conscious awareness at the moment of swearing.
Exhaustive counting supplies a durable external record of enacted falsehood.
Loss from memory limits the perpetrators' knowledge across time.
Presence with observation supplies the counter-memory that remains when they forget.

structural_cues: 58:6 sequences reporting their deeds, God's counting, their forgetting, and God's witness.
58:14 closes the oath scene with their present knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies present knowing, later forgetting, exhaustive counting, and witness; I infer a temporal asymmetry between tactical awareness and preserved accountability. The alternative is that 58:6 describes a broader class and need not diagnose these particular swearers' future memory.

changed_reading.before: 'While they know' indicates complete and stable awareness.
changed_reading.after: Their knowledge is culpably sufficient but short-horizon: they know what they are doing while an external witness preserves what they may later lose.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated alerting opener links observation to a recurring communication pattern: prohibited private counsel returns, then the same medium is explicitly permitted for truthful good. The focus oath becomes another publicly detectable output of a covert protocol, condemned not for privacy alone but for recurrent, knowingly false content and its alliance function.

activation_trace.role: The focus alert summons recognition of the oath-backed affiliation as a case.
The oath is the overt speech event through which the hidden alignment becomes legible.
The earlier identical alerting formula establishes a sequence of cases meant to be recognized.
Return after departure makes the bad communication recurrent rather than incidental.
Secret consultation supplies the concealed communication channel surrounding the repeated misconduct.
The same private channel appears with both prohibited and commanded contents, preventing privacy itself from carrying the blame.
Truth that passes into action supplies the positive content against which the focus's knowingly false oath is judged.

structural_cues: The formula 'have you not seen' occurs at 58:7, 58:8, and 58:14.
58:8 sequences prohibition, return, private counsel, altered greeting, and inward speech; 58:9 then assigns opposite moral contents to private counsel.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated opener, return to secret counsel, morally contrasting counsel, and the later oath; I infer that the opener trains pattern recognition across speech practices. The live alternative is that the 58:8 and 58:14 actors are only analogous cases, not one communication network.

changed_reading.before: The opening is a generic command to notice a single act of hypocrisy.
changed_reading.after: The opening asks the reader to recognize a recurring speech protocol whose hidden channel is morally neutral but whose returned false content discloses the alliance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent sequel literalizes oaths as a protective shield and immediately links that cover to diversion. The knowingly false oath in the focus therefore does defensive work: it absorbs scrutiny and creates operating room for conduct that turns people away.

activation_trace.role: The focus oath supplies the speech instrument later redescribed materially.
Its false content explains why the instrument needs to protect rather than disclose.
The oath sense identifies the very speech acts taken up as equipment.
The protecting shield image gives the oaths their defensive and concealing function.
Turning away and diverting supplies the action enabled by the oath-cover.

structural_cues: 58:16 follows the focus and its punishment notice, then sequences taking oaths as a shield before diversion from God's path.
The focus already joins oath, false content, and conscious knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the oath-as-shield image and its sequence before diversion; I infer the arrow shielded credibility enables obstruction and apply it back to the adjacent focus oath. An alternative is that the shield denotes social or legal immunity without emphasizing concealment.

changed_reading.before: The false oath tries to persuade its immediate hearers.
changed_reading.after: The false oath is defensive infrastructure: it covers the actors long enough for their obstructive alignment to operate.

context_deltas.mechanism: At resurrection the same actors swear to God just as they swear to the present audience and suppose they stand on something. The focus oath is thus not a one-off lie but a rehearsed posture whose performance can sustain self-miscalculation even while the speaker knows the immediate assertion is false.

activation_trace.role: The present oath supplies the behavior explicitly carried into the later audience comparison.
Immediate knowledge prevents the repeated posture from being reduced to innocent error.
Rousing the still supplies the radically changed setting in which the same oath behavior reappears.
Repeated swearing to two audiences makes the focus act a portable and rehearsed script.
Supposition supplies the self-credit produced alongside deliberate false performance.
The final liar designation fixes continuity between the present lie and the later posture.

structural_cues: 58:18 directly compares their swearing to God with their swearing to the present audience.
The later sequence joins that comparison to supposing they are on something and then identifies them as the liars.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit cross-audience comparison, resurrection, supposition, and the liar label; I infer that repeated oath-performance has become a portable posture that feeds self-miscalculation. The alternative is a fresh oath of desperation at judgment rather than an ingrained script.

changed_reading.before: They knowingly tell one strategic lie to a human audience.
changed_reading.after: They rehearse an oath posture that survives a total change of audience, allowing conscious falsehood and deeper self-miscalculation to coexist.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus presents tawalli as enacted allegiance; the sequel redescribes its mature state as domination that causes forgetting and gathers people into a party formed around a shared position. The 'neither/nor' group is therefore not neutral space but a transition into a rival factional identity.

activation_trace.role: Alliance and support supply the initially enacted alignment.
The group image supplies the social body toward which the alignment moves.
Domination, seizure, and gathering convert chosen proximity into captured agency.
Loss of remembrance supplies the cognitive displacement produced by domination.
A group consolidated around one view supplies the factional endpoint of the alignment.

structural_cues: 58:19 sequences seizure, caused forgetting of God's remembrance, and a repeated party designation.
58:14 places allegiance to a qawm before the denial that the actors belong to either named side.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies domination, caused forgetting, and party formation; I infer a process arrow from allegiance through cognitive capture to factional consolidation. The alternative is that 58:19 states the final classification without explaining how the focus tawalli began.

changed_reading.before: They voluntarily maintain an ambiguous alliance outside both groups.
changed_reading.after: Their liminality is transitional: allegiance becomes capture, capture displaces remembrance, and displacement consolidates a rival faction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final social contrast defines a qawm by faith and refuses loving alignment with those who set themselves across God's boundary, even when the opposing relation is the intimate body of one's clan. This sharpens the focus's 'neither of you nor of them': attempted dual belonging fails where allegiance crosses the community's constitutive boundary.

activation_trace.role: Love, support, and alliance supply the focus relation tested by the final contrast.
The hostile people supply the collective pole selected by the actors.
The believing people supply a corporate identity defined by a contrary alignment.
Love and attachment expose the affective core shared with patronage and alliance.
Opposition and mutual boundary-setting identify the fault line across which loving allegiance cannot be neutral.
Clan and kindred supply the strongest inherited collective claim that the allegiance boundary can override.

structural_cues: 58:22 begins with a qawm defined by belief and denies loving alignment with those opposing God and the messenger.
The same ayah enumerates fathers, sons, brothers, and clan before naming God's party, while 58:14 denies the actors membership in either side.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two qawm labels, affective attachment, opposition, and an escalating kin list; I infer that the focus double negation marks a failed attempt to inhabit both allegiance structures. A live alternative is that 'neither of you nor them' exposes hypocrisy specifically and is not a general account of communal membership.

changed_reading.before: The actors occupy an ambiguous position between two preexisting groups.
changed_reading.after: Their ambiguity is itself a failed membership strategy: affective-political allegiance crosses a constitutive boundary that can outweigh even inherited clan identity.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the branch-distant image of a colored garment that lies by its condition. It remains anchored in the focus's kidhb, invited seeing, and denied membership, but downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for performed appearance, not as the lexical sense of al-kadhib here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أَلَمْ تَرَ ... مَا هُم مِّنكُمْ وَلَا مِنْهُمْ ... ٱلْكَذِبِ

activation_trace.role: The ornamented cloth that misreports its own condition supplies a material image for false social presentation.
Visible appearance and reflected presentation make the false membership claim something displayed for inspection.
A distinguishing mark supplies the status-sign that the actors knowingly manipulate.

changed_reading.before: The falsehood is only a proposition uttered under oath.
changed_reading.after: The oath resembles a patterned status-garment: it displays belonging to observers while its wearers know that no underlying membership supports the display.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it crosses the hard-hide branch of ghadab with the later literal shield image. It remains anchored in the focus's wrath-marked group, proximity, and oath, and in 58:16's protective cover; downstream prose should qualify it as a material model of defensive affiliation, never as a claim that divine wrath lexically means hide or armor.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: تَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم ... وَيَحْلِفُونَ

activation_trace.role: Hard or folded hide supplies the material surface around which a defensive affiliation can be imagined.
Nearness without a separating gap places the actors against that hard social surface.
The explicit protecting shield lets the focus's oath and hard-surface images join as defensive cover.

changed_reading.before: They approach an angered group and separately swear a lie.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they press against a hardened social surface and fold oath-speech around the affiliation as protective cover.

strongest_changes: The denied motherhood relation in 58:2 turns the focus oath into attempted relational counterfeiting, not merely inaccurate speech.
58:16 and 58:18 turn the oath into both defensive infrastructure and a rehearsed posture that persists when its audience changes.
58:19 and 58:22 recast the neither/nor position as a movement from capture into faction and as a failed attempt at dual belonging across a constitutive allegiance boundary.
summary.what_was_special: The context repeatedly converts speech from content into social machinery: formulas try to assign relations, private channels recur, oaths protect operations, and allegiance consolidates into party membership.
remaining_uncertainties: The repeated opener supports pattern linkage, but the packet does not force the 58:8 secret-counsel actors and the 58:14 swearers to be one network.
The double negation may mark social liminality, rhetorical disavowal, or specifically hypocritical double affiliation.
The garment and hard-cover outliers are controlled material analogies, not proposed contextual senses of the roots.
